**Here are 8 high-signal posts** from the specified date range (all from 2026-08-07) matching the topic of AI agents transacting onchain, agent payments, AI-judged bounties, or decentralized AI oracles. I prioritized launches, demos, infrastructure details, and verifiable claims over general discussion. Selected from keyword + semantic searches (Latest mode, min engagement filter applied where possible).

1. **@osldotcom**  
   AgentPay enables developer AI agents to execute autonomous, intent-based payment flows to meet high-frequency, micro-value A2A demands.  
   Available for API integration today, developers simply express the payment intent—Amount, Asset, and Payee—while AgentPay instantly handles the complex routing, signing, and settlement.

2. **@osldotcom**  
   Today, we are turning that vision into reality with the launch of OSL AgentPay. 🤖  
   AgentPay gives developers a single API for autonomous, intent-based AI payments. It supports multiple stablecoins (USDT, USDC, USDGO) and emerging protocols (x402, AP2) while handling all the complex routing, signing, and settlement behind the scenes.  
   **Date posted:** 2026-08-07  
   **Engagement:** Likes=2, Retweets=0, Replies=1  
   **Link:** https://x.com/osldotcom/status/2085662067001032934

3. **@Spaulhrx**  
   Why AI Agents Need Their Own Wallets  
   An AI agent can analyze data, generate strategies, and make decisions.  
   But without a wallet, it still depends on a human to execute every action.  
   That changes the moment an agent can securely own and control onchain assets. It can pay for services, receive rewards, interact with protocols and coordinate with other agents without waiting for manual approval every step of the way.  
   Of course, autonomy alone isn’t enough. Every action needs to be transparent, verifiable, and governed by rules that users can trust.  
   That’s where @ritualnet comes in  
   Ritual provides the infrastructure for AI native applications where intelligence and execution exist in the same environment. Agents don’t just think. They can act onchain while remaining accountable through blockchain’s trust guarantees.  
   The future of AI isn’t just smarter models.  
   It’s autonomous agents with the ability to own, transact, and build onchain  
   **Date posted:** 2026-08-07  
   **Engagement:** Likes=7, Retweets=0, Replies=5  
   **Link:** https://x.com/Spaulhrx/status/2085797224559292440

4. **@AlexanderXQ_**  
   The Next Evolution of Payments Is Agentic — And https://b.ai/ Is Building for It  
   The next major step in digital payments may not be about making human payments faster.  
   It is about enabling AI agents to pay, transact, and settle value on their own.  
   This is where agentic payments become powerful.  
   Imagine an AI agent that needs to access data, purchase a digital service, call an API, rent computing resources, or interact with another machine. Instead of stopping to ask a human for approval every time a payment is required, the agent can execute the transaction programmatically and settle it directly on-chain.  
   That is the direction being explored through x402-based payment rails on TRON, with https://t.co/chbgEmnXBP, MERX, Oobit, and dTelecom contributing to an emerging infrastructure for machine-to-machine payments.  
   **Date posted:** 2026-08-07  
   **Engagement:** Likes=1, Retweets=0, Replies=0  
   **Link:** https://x.com/AlexanderXQ_/status/2085590733759631752

5. **@0xBANDAL**  
   AI agents are going to need more than just models and compute  
   They need reliable information coming from outside the chain if they are actually going to make decisions and act on them  
   That makes Rituals approach to enshrined oracles pretty interesting  
   Instead of having every application depend on another external layer for data and AI related inputs, some of that functionality can live much closer to the protocol  
   The more capable these agents become, the more important this part is going to be  
   An agent that can only see what is already onchain is still pretty limited  
   @ritualnet @ritualfnd  
   **Date posted:** 2026-08-07  
   **Engagement:** Likes=4, Retweets=1, Replies=1  
   **Link:** https://x.com/0xBANDAL/status/2085834414714749228

6. **@teohaik**  
   We talk a lot about AI agents becoming economic actors.  
   But for that to work, an agent needs more than an API.  
   It needs to be able to hold assets, sign transactions, make small payments, invoke services, and verify the result, all programmatically.  
   That is where blockchains get interesting for agents.  
   @SuiNetwork in particular has a useful combination here: programmable assets, low latency execution, predictable fees, and a model that maps quite naturally to objects and services.  
   The interesting question now is what agents will start paying each other for.  
   **Date posted:** 2026-08-07  
   **Engagement:** Likes=35, Retweets=3, Replies=2  
   **Link:** https://x.com/teohaik/status/2085665861130485934

7. **@AmpleProtocol**  
   .@Cloudflare is rolling out wallets for AI agents 🤖  
   Agents get stablecoin wallets with spending limits so they can pay for APIs, data and content on their own. Machine to machine, pay per use.  
   Here's the part for creators 🚨 An agent can only pay you if it can read who owns the work and what it costs.  
   That is licensing onchain. Your terms, public and machine readable, so the next wave of buyers doesn't need a human to say yes.  
   The buyers are becoming robots. Get your terms onchain LG ⚡

   Most "agentic payments" are still PowerPoint.  
   @xdcaitech just had order and pay for a coffee autonomously.  
   No human approval.  
   No API keys.  
   No billing portal.  
   Under the hood:  
   • x402 turns HTTP into a payment protocol  
   • Gasless USDC via EIP-3009  
   • Non-custodial smart wallets  
   • Native MCP support (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex)  
   Ai agents are about to become the internet's next big user base. but they can't fill out a credit card form or type in a cvv.  
   they need money that speaks their language natively.
